newsitem.title: INDIA: One woman killed, 12 wounded in Kashmir attacks.
newsitem.headline: One woman killed, 12 wounded in Kashmir attacks.

text.p: A woman was killed and at least 12 people were wounded on Tuesday in two grenade attacks on Indian security forces in Kashmir, authorities said.
Suspected militants lobbed a grenade at a paramilitary patrol and opened fire near Dal Lake in Srinagar, summer capital of Jammu and Kashmir state, police said.
A civilian woman was killed and two paramilitary police were among the wounded, they said.
Two Indian soldiers were wounded when separatists fired grenades at an army camp, an army spokesman said. The guerrillas launched four grenades at the army camp at Tatoo Ground in Srinagar, he said.
The attack came during a general strike called by the All Parties Hurriyat Conference, which groups about 30 separatist organisations.
The Hurriyat called the strike in protest against the deaths of four separatist leaders in a shootout with Indian forces last week.
The dead guerrillas belonged to the Hizb-ul Mujahideen, a hardline militant group among dozens fighting for independence or merger of Kashmir with neighbouring Pakistan, which disputes the region.
Police used teargas and batons on Tuesday to disperse demonstrators protesting against the Hizb-ul Mujahideen militants' deaths.
The army spokesman said soldiers had discovered a guerrilla hideout under floorboards at a Kashmir school where dozens could take shelter.

He said the army raided the hideout at Ratnipora in the Pulwama district of Kashmir following the interrogation of a Hizb-ul Mujahideen militant on Monday. As many as 50 guerrillas could fit in the space under the floor, authorities said.
Pulwama district is 32 km (20 miles) north of Srinagar.

India and Pakistan have fought two wars over Kashmir since independence from Britain in 1947. Pakistan denies Indian charges that it arms guerrillas who launched a major offensive against New Delhi in 1990.
Police and hospital officials say more than 20,000 people have been killed in the seven-year-old rebellion in Jammu and Kashmir, mainly Hindu India's only Moslem majority state.
